title: HTML Entity Parser
spaceBreakdown:
- string result: up to n chars - not counted (returned output)
- int n, int i: O(1)
- no recursion, no other containers
approach: All six HTML entities start with '&' and end with ';'. We scan the input left to right, building the output string. When we encounter '&', we check whether the upcoming substring matches any of the six known entities (using `string::compare` with bounds checks). If it matches, we append the replacement character and skip past the entire entity; otherwise we append '&' as a regular character and advance by one. Each character is visited exactly once, giving linear time.
hints: What two characters bookend every one of the six entities? The string may contain any of the 256 ASCII characters, so '&' can appear outside entities.
Single-pass string scan with direct substring comparison. In Example 1, at index 0 we see '&', compare text[0..4] to "&", it matches, so we output '&' and advance 5 positions.

```
i = 0
while i < n:
    if text[i] == '&':
        if text[i..i+5] matches """: output '"'; i += 6
        else if text[i..i+5] matches "'": output '\''; i += 6
        else if text[i..i+4] matches "&": output '&'; i += 5
        else if text[i..i+3] matches ">": output '>'; i += 4
        else if text[i..i+3] matches "<": output '<'; i += 4
        else if text[i..i+6] matches "⁄": output '/'; i += 7
        else: output '&'; i += 1
    else:
        output text[i]; i += 1
```

**No semicolon** - entity without closing ';' should not be replaced
`Input: "&amp"` → `Expected: "&amp"`
⚠️ Bug: matching only "&amp" (4 chars) without requiring ';' → returns "&"

**Bare ampersand at end** - single '&' with no following characters
`Input: "x&"` → `Expected: "x&"`
⚠️ Bug: reading text[i+1..i+4] without checking i+len <= n → undefined behavior or crash

**Non-entity ampersand word** - '&' followed by text that starts like an entity but diverges
`Input: "&ambassador;"` → `Expected: "&ambassador;"`
⚠️ Bug: matching only the first 3 characters "&am" for & → returns "&mbassador;"

**Consecutive entities** - entities back-to-back with no separator
`Input: "<>"` → `Expected: "<>"`
⚠️ Bug: incrementing i by 1 instead of by the entity length after a match → returns "<lt;>gt;"

followUps.q: What if the set of entities is provided at runtime as a list of (entity, replacement) pairs?
followUps.a: Store them in an unordered_map<string, char>. When you see '&', scan forward to the next ';' (or up to max entity length), extract the candidate, and look it up. TC stays O(n) since each character is still visited once; SC becomes O(k) for the map where k is the number of entities.

followUps.q: What if entities can be nested, e.g., "&quot;" should become '"' after two passes?
followUps.a: Run the same single-pass parser repeatedly until no replacement occurs in a pass. Each pass shrinks the string, so at most O(n/5) passes are needed. TC becomes O(n²/5) in the worst case; SC stays O(n) for the working string.

followUps.q: What if the input is a stream and you cannot store the entire string in memory?
followUps.a: Maintain a small ring buffer of size 7 (the longest entity). When you see '&', buffer characters until you hit ';' or exceed 7 characters, then decide whether to flush the replacement or the buffered text. TC is O(n); SC drops to O(1) auxiliary (the 7-byte buffer).
